builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LinQuant: Functional Invariances for Low-Precision Linear Recurrences
summary: LinQuant replaces naive low-precision quantization of dense matrix multiplications in chunkwise-parallel recurrent prefill (as in the SSDi8 pipeline for Mamba-2) by applying functional invariances—rotations, diagonal rescalings, and relocated decay/write factors—that preserve full-precision computation while making operands more quantization-friendly. It costs additional framework complexity and is restricted to recurrence families (linear, gated, delta-rule) where the seven invariances remain mathematically valid, requiring integration into a low-precision prefill pipeline. Adoption can fail if the production model uses a recurrence family or variant where the invariances do not hold, or if quantization fragility persists because the transformations do not sufficiently improve operand distributions for a given checkpoint.
rationale: The method targets low-precision prefill for recurrent/hybrid architectures, which is relevant to the reader's inference constraints, but it requires the specific workload of running Mamba-2/Nemotron-style models with a modifiable INT8 prefill pipeline, so it should be tracked and validated only if that workload is present.
technique: Invariance-based low-precision quantization for recurrent prefill

claims.statement: LinQuant replaces naive low-precision quantization of dense matrix multiplications in chunkwise-parallel recurrent prefill (as in the SSDi8 pipeline for Mamba-2) by applying functional invariances—rotations, diagonal rescalings, and relocated decay/write factors—that preserve full-precision computation while making operands more quantization-friendly. It costs additional framework complexity and is restricted to recurrence families (linear, gated, delta-rule) where the seven invariances remain mathematically valid, requiring integration into a low-precision prefill pipeline. Adoption can fail if the production model uses a recurrence family or variant where the invariances do not hold, or if quantization fragility persists because the transformations do not sufficiently improve operand distributions for a given checkpoint.
LinQuant improves perplexity at matched latency on Mamba-2 1.3B, 2.7B, and 8B and Nemotron-H 8B.
